title: Backup & DR: RPO, RTO, and Key Rules

scenes.line1: How much data can you lose?
scenes.line2: And how fast are you back?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how much data you can afford to lose, and how quickly you need to recover after a disaster?

scenes.label: RPO
scenes.sub: Max data you can lose in a disaster.
scenes.say: First up, RPO. That's your recovery point objective. It means the maximum data you can lose if things go wrong.

scenes.label: RTO
scenes.sub: How fast you must restore service.
scenes.say: Next, RTO. That's your recovery time objective. It's how quickly you have to get everything running again.
Follow the three-two-one rule: three copies of your data, on two types of media, with one offsite. This keeps you safe from most disasters.

scenes.label: Immutable
scenes.sub: Backups can't be changed or deleted.
scenes.say: Immutable backups can't be changed or deleted. They're your best defense against ransomware.

scenes.question: What's the first thing to ask in DR?
scenes.right: Start with RPO and RTO: data loss and recovery time.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Don't start with backup size. Always ask about RPO and RTO first—how much data loss and how fast you must recover.
